svg.title: MLLM architecture, multi-head attention block, and overall gain diagram
svg.desc: The figure is organized into three main base frames: left MLLM architecture with stacked transformer layers and token inputs; middle multi-head attention block with standard MHA computations, visual attention ratio, reasoning/perception gating branches, and flowing standard procedure; right overall gain comparison with two layer-head grids, legend, and conclusion arrows. Content is constructed in native SVG with stable semantic IDs. No SAM assets are available.

g.title: MLLM Architecture
g.desc: Origin is the transformer stack; upward conduction reaches text response, downward reaches image/text token sequence, while residual arrows and plus nodes connect each layer.

g.title: Multi-Head Attention Block
g.desc: Origin is the standard MHA region. Computation proceeds left-to-right through Q/K/V matrices, scaling, attention, output matrices, then downward to visual attention ratio and the reasoning/perception gating branches. The two lower branches are horizontally aligned and symmetric except for thresholds and gate outcomes.

g.title: Overall Gain from Our Method
g.desc: Origin is the upper layer-head grid. Downward conduction compares the improved grid. Rightward conduction explains that a misallocated most-dominating attention head causes hallucinated answer, while a well allocated dominating head leads to the correct final answer.
